Yes, the appellate court will likely reverse the first-degree felony-murder conviction. Most jurisdictions limit felony murder to deaths of innocent persons, and the "universal proximate cause" claim in the team note is wrong. Many states still use the agency theory, and even under proximate cause most courts won't extend liability to a co-felon's death, which the felony-murder rule's purpose of deterring danger to innocents doesn't cover. The man can still be convicted of armed robbery, conspiracy and assault, and in some proximate-cause states a minority might uphold a lesser homicide charge.

CONFIDENCE: 82
